blocks.title: Review: “Small Questions, Large Answers”
paras: In *Small Questions, Large Answers*, the (fictional) philosopher Ines Varga **takes ten everyday puzzles** (Should I **return** the extra change? Is it **rude** to **ghost** a friend?) and **treats each as a window** onto a **major theory**. The result is **warm, witty and, for the most part, rigorous**.

Varga **writes with the lightest of touches**; her examples **land**. Yet **lightness has a price**: the chapter on moral luck **gives the impression** of settling a **debate that is far from settled**, and her **dismissal** of virtue ethics is **too brisk** to **convince**.
**Even so**, this is **a commendable introduction**. Readers who **come for the anecdotes** will **stay for the arguments**. **Recommended**, with **a pinch of salt**.

items.q: The reviewer finds the book entirely unrigorous.
The review calls the dismissal of virtue ethics too brisk.
The reviewer recommends the book with reservations.

blocks.body: Resenha de divulgação: **descreva**, **elogie**, **ressalve** (*yet, even so*) e **recomende** (*with a pinch of salt*). Use **the + adjetivo superlativo** para efeito: *the lightest of touches*.
*Brisk* é positivo para ritmo, mas negativo para tratamento de um tema complexo (*too brisk*).

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence review of a real or imaginary book of popular philosophy.
blocks.model: This lively book takes five everyday dilemmas and treats each as a window onto an old debate. The author writes with the lightest of touches. Yet lightness has a price: the final chapter is too brisk to convince. Even so, it is a commendable introduction. Readers who come for the stories will stay for the ideas. Recommended, with a pinch of salt.
